nodes.description: p62 is a multidomain scaffold: an N-terminal PB1 oligomerisation domain, a TRAF6-binding region, an LC3-interacting region (LIR) that docks it to the forming autophagosome, a KEAP1-interacting region (KIR), and a C-terminal UBA domain that binds ubiquitinated cargo. PDB-associated variants cluster in and around the UBA domain, whereas ALS/FTD-associated variants are distributed across the protein, including the LIR and KIR. Several alleles, p.Pro392Leu above all, occur in both groups. Which presentation an allele produces is therefore only partly predicted by where it lies.

nodes.description: p62 links ubiquitinated proteins to LC3 on the forming autophagosome so they can be degraded. Disease variants reduce LC3B recognition (LIR variants such as p.Leu341Val), reduce TBK1/ULK1-dependent phosphorylation of the UBA domain that activates cargo binding, or remove the UBA domain (the c.1165+1G>A splice product). The shared result is slower autophagic clearance of ubiquitinated proteins, the lesion the neurodegenerative and myopathic presentations are thought to share with VCP-, OPTN- and TBK1-related disease.

nodes.description: Stress granules are transient ribonucleoprotein condensates that must be disassembled, partly by autophagy, once stress resolves. Mutant or depleted p62 slows their clearance. The TIA1 p.Asn357Ser variant enhances TIA1 phase separation, and granules made with it persist, bind more p62 and accumulate ubiquitinated and aggregated proteins. Co-expression of mutant TIA1 and mutant SQSTM1 in myoblasts is synergistically toxic, which is the proposed basis of the digenic myopathy.
